note.after_visit_summary: You sprained your right ankle during basketball practice. It is swollen and bruised on the outside, and hurts when you walk. The exam shows a mild to moderate ligament sprain, and no fracture is suspected based on your symptoms and exam. You should ice your ankle for 15 to 20 minutes every 2 to 3 hours for the next two days, keep it elevated on a pillow, and wear a compression wrap. We will fit you with a lace-up ankle brace to wear during sports for the next couple of months. Take ibuprofen 400 mg by mouth every 8 hours with food for 5 to 7 days, then only as needed for pain. You may use crutches for 2 to 3 days if walking hurts, but try to put weight on it as tolerated. Do ankle alphabet exercises (trace letters with your toes) a few times each day. Avoid basketball for about two weeks. You can return when you can hop and run without pain. If you cannot bear weight or pain moves to the bone, call us for a possible x-ray. If not improved in two weeks, return for possible physical therapy. We will send a note to Coach Brennan and for gym class at Westfield High School. No known allergies to medications except Bactrim, which causes a rash. You are not currently taking any daily medications.
